description: sevdesk tags. Read is GET /Tag (records wrapped in `objects`), full refresh only — Model_TagResponse carries no `update` field and sevdesk documents no updateAfter/createAfter filter on this operation, so there is no incremental cursor. Two structural oddities are authored deliberately: (1) insert has no plain POST /Tag — creation is reachable only through the factory route POST /Tag/Factory/create, whose body REQUIRES `object`, so a tag cannot be created standalone but only attached to an existing Invoice, Voucher, Order or CreditNote; that route also answers with the TagRelation shape (Model_TagCreateResponse), not the read record, so the created tag's own id sits at `tag.id`. (2) PUT /Tag/{tagId} answers with a bare Model_TagResponse — the spec declares no `objects` wrapper on the update, unlike GET — so the upsert reads its generated key straight off `response.body.id`. The spec spells the update path param `{tagId}`; it is authored `{tag_id}` to satisfy the snake_case placeholder constraint.

id.description: Filter by the sevdesk id of the tag. Declared `type: number` by sevdesk's GET /Tag parameter list and authored verbatim, even though the read model serializes the record's own `id` as a JSON string.

name.description: Filter by tag name. Filterable, but not documented as unique, so it is not usable as a conflict key.

schema.description: GET /Tag response envelope. Records are wrapped in `objects`; a top-level `total` is added only when countAll=true, which this endpoint does not send.

id.description: Unique identifier of the tag (system-set). Declared `type: string` by Model_TagResponse; the numeric value is serialized as a JSON string on the wire (spec example '1').

objectName.description: Model name; always 'Tag'. Not declared as an enum in the spec, but its description pins the constant.

additionalInformation.description: Additional information on the tag. Declared `type: string, default: null`.

create.description: Creation timestamp (system-set, readOnly). sevdesk emits offset-carrying ISO-8601 across its models (e.g. 2024-06-28T14:42:58+02:00). The only temporal field on this model — Model_TagResponse declares no `update`, unlike nearly every other sevdesk model.

name.description: Name of the tag (readOnly on the response model).

sevClient.description: Client relation the tag belongs to ({id, objectName='SevClient'}); filled automatically by sevdesk.

schema.description: One POST /Tag/Factory/create payload. sevdesk documents NO plain POST /Tag — the /Tag path item declares `get` only — so this non-RESTful factory route is the sole create path, and its `object` member is required: a tag cannot be created standalone, only attached to an existing Invoice, Voucher, Order or CreditNote. The route's 200 body is Model_TagCreateResponse (the TagRelation shape, objectName 'TagRelation'), which is NOT the read record shape; the created tag's own id is therefore read from `tag.id`, not `id`.

object.description: The document the new tag is attached to. Required by the factory route — there is no standalone tag creation.

id.description: Id of the invoice/order/voucher/creditNote the tag is attached to.

objectName.description: Model name of the attached document.

schema.description: PUT /Tag/{tagId} (spec spelling; authored {tag_id}) updates an existing tag. sevdesk declares exactly one updatable property — `name` — so the request body carries only that; `id` is present solely to address the record and supplies the path segment. The provider documents no natural key beyond the tag id (`name` is filterable but nowhere documented as unique), so this mode matches on the provider-assigned id.

id.description: sevdesk id of the tag to update; supplies the {tag_id} path segment. The path parameter is declared integer by the spec, while the read model serializes id as a string.

name.description: The new name of the tag — the only property PUT /Tag/{tagId} accepts.
